title: Heterogeneous inference digest — routing, kernels, and quick experiments
content:
Purpose: sketch out reading notes + tactical experiment ideas for heterogeneous inference (mix of GPU types, CPU fallback, quantized variants). Mostly scribbles for sprint planning and follow-ups.

Top-level takeaways:
- Routing policy matters more than I expected for mixed-capacity clusters: latency SLOs can be preserved by conservative pinning for p99-critical flows and probabilistic spillover for bulk batch workloads.
- Kernel selection + micro-batching interplay: some kernels (flash-attn-like) give huge throughput wins at medium sequence lengths but cost us warm-up latency for tiny requests. Need per-route heuristics.
- Quantized variants are not plug-and-play: observed non-linear quality drops on few-shot prompts; need a small evaluation harness per model variant.

Papers / notes to self:
- MoE inference at scale (paper A): interesting stateless routing but complex KV cache invalidation when experts are sharded. TODO: simulate expert hotspotting with synthetic request mix.
- Dynamic kernel selection (paper B): shows gains when switching kernels at 128/256 token thresholds. Could integrate into runtime: kernel_candidates + threshold table.
- KV-shard eviction strategies: LRU is ok but misses long-tail conversational recency; look into frequency-weighted eviction.

Experiment ideas (fast wins):
1) Small harness: 3 model variants (fp16, int8, 4-bit) + two hardware tiers (A100, T4). Run identical prompt set (200 prompts with variable lengths) and capture p50/p95/p99 latency, perplexity change, token-loss-like score. Flag any int8 > 2% quality regression.
2) Routing policy A/B: (A) strict capacity-aware pinning vs (B) probabilistic spill + fallback queue. Measure tail latency and observed cost.
3) Kernel threshold table: instrument runtime to record per-request sequence length distribution and switch kernel at observed inflection. Start with naive thresholds from paper B.

Unresolved questions / open concerns:
- How to do online detection of quality regressions for quantized variants without large eval sets? Maybe use synthetic prompt mutations + small reference set per customer route.
- Can we incrementally warm KV caches for cold variants during rollout (cheap partial rebuild)? Explore partial-restore from hot variant.
- Autoscaler interactions: burst policies + dedicated pools sometimes fight; need a simple contract for graceful degradation.

Quick links (to read later):
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00027  # placeholder MoE implementation notes
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11171  # dynamic kernel thresholds 
- https://github.com/flash-attention/flash-attention  # implementation to poke at

TODOs / next steps:
- Prep small benchmark harness (1 week): implement experiment 1 locally on dev cluster.
- Sync with SRE: define expected behavior for spillover. Add to sprint board.
- Draft short proposal for rollout strategy of quantized variants (2–3 pages) with eval checklist.

Notes to self: keep results reproducible + document exact seed prompts. Don't conflate model architecture differences with runtime-induced artifacts (e.g., batching-induced timing).

Random scribbles:
- Could we have a per-customer micro-eval that runs a 50 prompt sanity check on variant changes? Lightweight, runs in background and flags regressions to console.
- Consider exposing a "quality meter" in console that shows rolling delta against baseline on representative prompts.

End of page.
